name: Oppida

large fortified settlements of the sixth to fifth centuries B.C.E.

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Oppida is an archaeological term. This Latin word describes fortified Celtic towns. La Tène in Switzerland is a famous example. The settlements of the sixth and fifth centuries B.C.E. stood on heights or promontories. They often lay near mineral deposits that supplied the settlement's wealth.

okr.objective: Oppida describes the fortified towns of the ancient Celts.
